nomenclature.etymology_html:
- Walsura : A Telugu and Tamil name for the plant.
- Trifoliolata : Tri-folium meaning trifoliate, having three leaflets.

stem_bark.text: The bark of Walsura trifoliolata is pale brown, longitudinally fissured and transversally cracked with age. The branches of Walsura trifoliolata are brittle. The branchlets are velvet-hairy.
stem_bark.text_html:
The bark of Walsura trifoliolata is pale brown, longitudinally fissured and transversally cracked with age.
The branches of Walsura trifoliolata are brittle. The branchlets are velvet-hairy.

seed.text: The seed of Walsura trifoliolata is enclosed into an ovoid stone . The stone is light brown-coloured and about 8 mm x 6 mm. There is one stone per fruit and each stone contains one seed.
seed.text_html: The seed of Walsura trifoliolata is enclosed into an ovoid stone. The stone is light brown-coloured and about 8 mm x 6 mm. There is one stone per fruit and each stone contains one seed.

fruit.text: The fruit of Walsura trifoliolata is an ovoid drupe . It is 1.5-2 cm long and 1-1.5 cm wide, tomentose with a solitary stone inside.
fruit.text_html:
The fruit of Walsura trifoliolata is an ovoid drupe. 
It is 1.5-2 cm long and 1-1.5 cm wide, tomentose with a solitary stone inside.

flower.text: The inflorescences of Walsura trifoliolata are terminal and axillary corymbose panicles up to 15 cm long with 5-8 cm long peduncles . The flowers of Walsura trifoliolata are pentamerous, creamy-white, 6-7 mm across with a 1 mm long pedicel . The calyx is composed of 5 lobes. These calyx-lobes are pubescent, yellow-greenish, triangular and about 1 mm long. The corolla is composed of 5 cream-coloured and puberulous petals . They are ovate-oblong with acute apex and about 2.5 mm long and 1.5 mm wide. There are 10 stamens . They are 1.5 mm long and connate at the base. The ovary is globose, 1.5-2 mm across and 2-locular with 2 ovules in each locule. The style is 1 mm long with a capitate stigma . The flowers are fragrant.
flower.text_html:
The inflorescences of Walsura trifoliolata are terminal and axillary corymbose panicles up to 15 cm long with 5-8 cm long peduncles.
The flowers of Walsura trifoliolata are pentamerous, creamy-white, 6-7 mm across with a 1 mm long pedicel.
The calyx is composed of 5 lobes. These calyx-lobes are pubescent, yellow-greenish, triangular and about 1 mm long.
The corolla is composed of 5 cream-coloured and puberulous petals. They are ovate-oblong with acute apex and about 2.5 mm long and 1.5 mm wide.
There are 10 stamens. They are 1.5 mm long and connate at the base.
The ovary is globose, 1.5-2 mm across and 2-locular with 2 ovules in each locule. The style is 1 mm long with a capitate stigma.
The flowers are fragrant.

leaf.text: The leaves of Walsura trifoliolata grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). Walsura trifoliata has trifoliate leaves. These compound leaves are about 8-15 cm long and wide. The leaves have a 2.5-4 cm long petiole . The leaflets are leathery and coriaceous and 5-9 cm long and 2.5-3.5 wide. They are elliptic with a obtuse-retuse apex , rounded-cuneate base and entire margins . The leaflets are glabrous, dark-green glossy above and light-green beneath with prominent midrib. The leaflets have a 4-5 mm long petiolule . The venation of the leaflets is reticulate.
leaf.text_html:
The leaves of Walsura trifoliolata grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged).
Walsura trifoliata has trifoliate leaves. These compound leaves are about 8-15 cm long and wide.
The leaves have a 2.5-4 cm long petiole.
The leaflets are leathery and coriaceous and 5-9 cm long and 2.5-3.5 wide. They are elliptic with a obtuse-retuse apex, rounded-cuneate base and entire margins.
The leaflets are glabrous, dark-green glossy above and light-green beneath with prominent midrib. The leaflets have a 4-5 mm long petiolule.
The venation of the leaflets is reticulate.

habit.text: Walsura trifoliolata is an evergreen and medium-sized tree (up to 12-15 meters) with a dense foliage and short bole. The young shoots and the branchlets are tomentose.
habit.text_html:
Walsura trifoliolata is an evergreen and medium-sized tree (up to 12-15 meters) with a dense foliage and short bole.
The young shoots and the branchlets are tomentose.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Walsura trifoliata is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. The seeds of Walsura trifoliata are dispersed by various fruit-eating birds and mammals.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Walsura trifoliata is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    The seeds of Walsura trifoliata are dispersed by various fruit-eating birds and mammals.

phenology.text: From Juanary to April. From May to October. From August to October. Evergreen foliage. ( This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains )
phenology.text_html:
• Flowering season :

    From Juanary to April.

  • Fruiting season :

    From May to October.

  • Seeding season :

    From August to October.

  • Leaves falling :

    Evergreen foliage.

    • (This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains)

reforestation.text: Walsura trifoliata is able to grow in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. The tree can be planted in half shade. This tree is propagated by seeds. 12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Walsura trifoliata is able to grow in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining. The tree can be planted in half shade.
    This tree is propagated by seeds.

  • Seed treatments :

    12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
